skill.name: fiftyone-find-duplicates
skill.description: Find duplicate and near-duplicate images in FiftyOne datasets using FiftyOne Brain similarity workflows.
skill.summary: Guides FiftyOne users through image deduplication with Brain similarity operators.
skill.author: AdonaiVera

security_audit.summary: All static external-command, network, and system-reconnaissance detections are false positives from Markdown examples, inline function names, local app URLs, and documentation links. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found. One semantic concern remains: install commands returned by tooling should be validated before any execution.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance asks the assistant to offer running install commands returned by MCP responses.
remediation.suggestion: Tell assistants to inspect and explain dependency commands, allow only expected package-manager commands, and require explicit user confirmation before execution.

content.value_statement: Duplicate and near-duplicate images can distort dataset quality and model training. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through FiftyOne Brain workflows to find, review, and remove redundant samples.
actual_capabilities: Set a FiftyOne dataset context and launch the app for delegated Brain operators.
Discover installed Brain plugin operators and inspect their current schemas.
Compute image similarity embeddings with configurable brain keys and models.
Find exact or near-duplicate images with practical threshold guidance.
Load duplicate views and filters for review in the FiftyOne App.
Run deduplication operators after review to keep representative samples.
limitations: Requires a running FiftyOne MCP server and the @voxel51/brain plugin.
Works with image datasets already loaded in FiftyOne, not standalone folders by itself.
Similarity computation can be slow for large datasets.
Deletion steps need careful review because they can remove dataset samples.

use_cases.title: Clean Image Training Sets
use_cases.description: Find redundant images before model training so validation and training data are less biased.

use_cases.title: Review Visual Redundancy
use_cases.description: Group visually similar samples and inspect representatives before changing the dataset.

use_cases.title: Remove Exact Duplicate Media
use_cases.description: Identify identical media files and use FiftyOne tools to keep one representative copy.

prompt_templates.title: Find Near Duplicates
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a known dataset name.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find near-duplicate images in my FiftyOne dataset named DATASET_NAME. Guide me through setup, similarity computation, duplicate discovery, and review.

prompt_templates.title: Review Duplicate Groups
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after duplicates have been detected.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to view all samples with near-duplicate group IDs in the FiftyOne App and inspect one group at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Exact Duplicates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup for identical media files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me find exact duplicate media files in my active FiftyOne dataset, review the result, and remove duplicates only after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Similarity Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for threshold and model selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare threshold choices for near-duplicate detection, choose a fast embedding model, and reuse the similarity index for later searches.

output_examples.input: Find near duplicates in my wildlife-images dataset.
output_examples.output: The assistant sets the dataset context, launches the FiftyOne App, checks Brain operators, computes similarity embeddings, and opens a duplicate review view.

output_examples.input: I have copied product photos in my dataset.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends exact duplicate detection first, then guides review before using a deduplication operator to keep representative samples.

output_examples.input: The threshold found too many similar images.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains distance-based thresholds and suggests trying stricter values before deleting any samples.

best_practices: Confirm the Brain plugin and operator schemas before running expensive jobs.
Start with the default near-duplicate threshold and adjust after visual review.
Review duplicate views before running any deduplication operator.
anti_patterns: Running deduplication before checking representatives in the app.
Recomputing embeddings with new brain keys when an existing similarity index is reusable.
Running dependency install commands from tool output without verification.

faq.question: Does this skill delete images automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides review steps and only describes deletion through FiftyOne deduplication operators after confirmation.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need a running FiftyOne MCP server and the @voxel51/brain plugin enabled.

faq.question: Can it find exact duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for exact duplicate media and near-duplicate visual matches.

faq.question: How does threshold selection work?
faq.answer: Lower distance thresholds find more similar images. The skill recommends starting at 0.3 for near duplicates.

faq.question: Can embeddings be reused?
faq.answer: Yes. A saved brain key can support repeated duplicate detection and similarity workflows.

faq.question: Does it work outside FiftyOne?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the images are loaded as samples in a FiftyOne dataset.
